title.es: Obligación: have to, don't have to, must, mustn't

objective: Al terminar expresas obligación y prohibición con have to, don't have to, must y mustn't y no los confundes.

warmup.prompt_es: 'No tienes que ir' y 'no debes ir' no significan lo mismo, y en inglés tampoco: don't have to ≠ mustn't.

lines.speaker: Mr Hill
lines.text: Welcome, Sara. Here are the main rules. You have to wear a uniform at work.
lines.es: Bienvenida, Sara. Estas son las reglas principales. Tienes que usar uniforme en el trabajo.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: Do I have to buy it?

lines.speaker: Mr Hill
lines.text: No, you don't have to. The company gives it to you. But you mustn't wear it outside work.
lines.es: No, no tienes que hacerlo. La empresa te lo da. Pero no debes usarlo fuera del trabajo.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: OK. Do I have to work on Saturdays?

lines.speaker: Mr Hill
lines.text: No, you don't. But you have to start at eight every day, and you must be on time.
lines.es: No. Pero tienes que empezar a las ocho todos los días, y debes ser puntual.

glossary.example: You have to wear a uniform.
You don't have to buy it.
You have to wear a uniform.

md_es: | **have to** | obligación (por una regla o situación externa) | *You have to wear a uniform.* |
| **don't have to** | **no es necesario** (tienes libertad) | *You don't have to buy it.* |
| **must** | obligación fuerte (personal o en reglas escritas) | *You must be on time.* |
**¡Cuidado!** *don't have to* = no hace falta; *mustn't* = está prohibido. *You don't have to come* (puedes no venir) ≠ *You mustn't come* (no debes venir).
**Preguntas:** *Do I have to work on Saturdays? — Yes, you do. / No, you don't.* (con *have to* se usa *do*; con *must* no: *Must I …?* suena formal).
**Pasado:** *must* no tiene pasado; se usa **had to**: *I had to wait for an hour.*
Pronunciación: *have to* /ˈhæf tə/ (la v suena /f/) · *mustn't* /ˈmʌsnt/ (la t no se pronuncia).

common_mistakes_es.wrong: You mustn't come if you don't want.
common_mistakes_es.right: You don't have to come if you don't want to.
common_mistakes_es.note: Para 'no hace falta' usa don't have to.

common_mistakes_es.right: I must go. / I have to go.
common_mistakes_es.note: Must va con verbo base, sin to.
